A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCEC research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and included appendices support reliable comparison; v1 Sections 7.1–7.2 correspond to v2 Appendices B and D.

before.justification: v1 reports original TCEC image-generation results on MJHQ and sDCI in Table 1 and OpenSora video-generation results on VBench in Table 2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds ablation results, inference timings and visual analyses in Tables 3–6 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: The two-step compensation, channel-wise scaling, regularized loss, coefficient solution and empirical regularization rule in Equations 13–18 remain unchanged. The DPM++ adaptation is retained in Appendix D. New ablations evaluate existing methodological choices without establishing a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The stated COCO and WebVid calibration data, MJHQ/sDCI image benchmarks and VBench video evaluation are retained. Additional Flux, CogVideoX and Wan measurements and visual examples remain within the existing image/video generation tasks; they expand model configurations and reported evidence without introducing distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 4–5 newly evaluate the full-history correction from Equation 10 and grid-search regularization as internal comparison alternatives to the selected TCEC configuration. Established baseline membership in Tables 1–2 is unchanged. GGUF already appears in v1 Figure 2, and the expanded quantizer-plus-TCEC labels do not introduce new external baselines.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce approximation and regularization controls, a four-step Flux W4A8 diagnostic with guidance scale 3.5, and timing configurations including 30-step Flux and 480P videos of specified lengths. The calibration counts, sampling settings and metrics for the retained main benchmarks remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C/Table 4 adds empirical testing of full-history versus two-step correction on SDXL and PixArt. Appendix F/Table 5 tests grid search against empirical regularization, while Appendix E/Figure 3 supplies stepwise error maps. These substantially expand evidence examining central approximations and error behavior that v1 mainly motivated through theory and prose.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Every numerical entry in the retained Tables 1–2 is unchanged. v2 adds results for central design controls and image/video inference overhead: Table 4 reports SDXL PSNR 26.1 versus 27.3 for Equations 10 and 13, and Table 3 reports Flux latency of 9.947 seconds for SVDQuant versus 9.996 with TCEC. Tables 5–6 and Figures 3–4 add further results; several reference rows reproduce existing Table 1 values.

T1.justification: Near Equations 21–22, v1 Section 7.1 asserts that sqrt(alpha_(t-1)/alpha_t) and rho_t are below one. v2 Appendix B removes these contraction assertions and retains a general bound by rho_t. Most of the proof, its m=1 conclusion and the solver derivation remain unchanged. Appendix G also adds a computational-complexity estimate.

C1.justification: The theoretical novelty, compensation, orthogonality and SOTA claims remain. The reported overhead claim tightens from at most 1% to 0.5%. The revised abstract highlights a 1.2-point SDXL PSNR advantage already present in v1's results and introduction.

C2.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 6's explicit limitation concerning error accumulation across layers within the denoising network. Appendix F adds tuning-cost arguments for empirical regularization. Its assertion that grid search offers no performance advantage is broader than Table 5 supports: grid search reports lower LPIPS, 0.090 versus 0.092.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the Nvidia A800-40G platform for its added timing measurements and specifies model versions, video lengths and diagnostic settings. Tables 1–2 explicitly identify SVDQuant+TCEC and ViDiT-Q+TCEC compositions. The previously documented quantization ranks, group size, coefficient calculation and calibration recipe remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 removes the ABQ-LLM and GQSA citations and reference entries, previously cited in Section 2.2. The remaining related-work discussion and positioning of TCEC relative to diffusion quantization research are substantially retained; conversion to author–date citations is stylistic.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and section order remain intact. Changes include author and contribution text, citation style, spelling corrections, the abstract ending and appendix cross-references. The former numbered supplement becomes lettered appendices, including a new LLM-usage disclosure, without extensive rewriting of the retained scientific narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables and two figures covering ablations, timings, error maps and qualitative examples. Table 1 moves from interrupting the method derivation into the experimental section, and Tables 1–2 gain expanded method labels. The author block, headings, typography and figure sizing are also reformatted, substantially changing the document's presentation.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–6 and Figure 3 provide concrete controls, error visualizations and timings supporting design and overhead claims that v1 largely asserted. This improves the paper's evidential support. The gain is tempered by removal of the within-network error limitation and Appendix F's overstatement of Table 5 despite grid search's lower reported LPIPS.
